messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU nodepool 'pool-west-1' autoscaler failed to scale — reached configured hard limit (max_nodes=120). queue_size=18,400; 95th_token_latency up 6x. paging oncall.
oncall-sre: taking this. tagging infra and cloud. @eva are you oncall for serving?
eva: I am. grabbing logs + checking autoscaler controller now.
infra-bot: scaler: reconcile loop error: reached nodepool max_nodes (120) — cannot provision more nodes. reason=MaxNodesConfigured
samir: can we confirm this is a config limit, not cloud quota? @maggie can you check provider quotas and nodepool settings?
eva: running quick check: `kubectl get nodepool pool-west-1 -o yaml` -> shows `spec.maxNodes: 120`. autoscaler "desired"=120, current=120. No provisioning errors from infra agent aside from limit.

```
# autoscaler status snippet
pool: pool-west-1
currentNodes: 120
desiredNodes: 120
maxNodes: 120
lastScaleReason: MaxNodesConfigured
```
customer-support: CS update: we have ~15 customer tickets for embeddings and generation timeouts; some 503s for enterprise customers in NA. Flagged top 3 customers for SRE exec.
julian: can we divert non-critical traffic to the fallback small-model endpoint or a different region? Need quick mitigation to reduce customer impact while we fix capacity.
eva: will start routing low-priority work to fallback endpoint and enable request throttling for repeated retries. posting quick swap command:
```
# route low-prio to fallback
redwood route set --pool pool-west-1 --priority low --fallback-model small-embed-v1
```
maggie: looked at cloud account — no provider hard quota hit. This is our cluster config `maxNodes=120`. I can do a manual nodepool resize to 180 but need quick approval from eng leads. Manual resize ETA ~8 minutes once started (nodes provision + kube join).
samir: approve manual bump to 180. go ahead @maggie. keep cost monitor on. :warning:
maggie: starting manual resize now. applying `spec.maxNodes=180` and issuing provider node create.
infra-bot: provider API events: 20 new instances requested, provisioning started, init scripts queued.
eva: will pause autoscaler reconciliation temporarily while manual join completes, then let it resume. also enabling bucketed token limits to protect latency-sensitive paths.
customer-support: continuing to patch customers; noticed 503 -> 429 pattern after throttling applied. fewer new incidents but some backlog still in queues.
maggie: provider reports new nodes healthy and joined. Kubernetes shows +58 nodes; node count=178. updating status.
```
# kubectl get nodes summary
Ready Nodes: 178
Pending Pods: 420
Queue Length (ingress): 1,200 -> down from 18,400
```
eva: autoscaler resumed; desired back to 150 then scaling down to steady state. queue drain in progress — estimates ~12 minutes to normal.
julian: good. left a temporary rule to route heavy embedding requests to smaller model for non-enterprise traffic to keep latency low.
customer-support: CS: major customers on watch; they acknowledged mitigation. no longer seeing new 503s from top-3 customers.
oncall-sre: summary: manual nodepool increase from 120->180 executed by @maggie; autoscaler resumed; backlog drained from ~18.4k -> ~1.2k -> steady. primary impact: increased latency and 503s for ~25 minutes during peak. tagging eng-runtime and infra for postmortem and follow-up.
samir: immediate action items: 1) revisit default maxNodes and scaling policy for pool-west-1, 2) add an emergency manual-runbook for cap raises, 3) evaluate cost guardrails for manual increases.
julian: add a routing policy that automatically shifts low-priority embedding traffic to smaller models when queue > X.
eva: will create the incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime + infra. adding initial timeline + logs.
oncall-sre: incident resolved — services back to normal, queue drained, autoscaler healthy. closing the page. :white_check_mark:
customer-support: thanks team. we'll send a short customer update and link to postmortem when ready.
